# Primary sources for recursive self modeling

Focused source map, checked 5 October 2026. This is a targeted investigation rather than a systematic review or an assertion of current consensus. Entries distinguish original experiments, formal work, original theoretical positions, and reviews. Papers support the claims stated beside them, not an overall theory of consciousness. Source copies and detailed working notes remain in this chat's work directory.

## Metacognition and introspective access

**Nelson and Narens 1990. Metamemory A theoretical framework and new findings.** Original framework with empirical material. Checked the chapter's monitoring/control definitions and discussion of levels, reports, and study allocation, especially pages 125–137. It supports separate measurement of monitoring and regulation. It does not establish anatomical tiers or accuracy at every level. [Author chapter](https://sites.socsci.uci.edu/~lnarens/1990/Nelson%26Narens_Book_Chapter_1990.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0079-7421(08)60053-5).

**Fleming and Daw 2017. Self Evaluation of Decision Making A General Bayesian Framework for Metacognitive Computation.** Original computational theory with simulations. Confidence is modeled as inference about a decision, potentially using different evidence across time or space; the actor's choice can itself be evidence. Checked the introductory model and model comparisons. This supports functional separation without proving separate brain structures for successive semantic levels. It is not a new experiment establishing the proposed architecture. [Full paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5178868/), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1037/rev0000045).

**Nisbett and Wilson 1977. Telling more than we can know Verbal reports on mental processes.** Critical review and theoretical argument. Checked the distinction between access to contents and explanations of the processes producing them, including pages 255–256. The paper supports caution about causal introspective explanations while acknowledging informational advantages from private contents and history. It does not establish that all introspection is false. [Original paper mirror](https://gwern.net/doc/psychology/cognitive-bias/illusion-of-depth/1977-nisbett.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.84.3.231).

**Ericsson and Simon 1980. Verbal reports as data.** Methodological theory and evidence review. It distinguishes reporting attended information from generating explanations and treats report validity as dependent on instructions and mechanisms. Access limitation: the original PDF was available but image-only extraction did not support a full-text audit; the authors' abstract and indexed excerpts were checked. This is a qualification of blanket skepticism, not a guarantee of transparent reporting. [Original PDF](https://acs.ist.psu.edu/ist597/papers/ericssonS80.pdf), [Abstract record](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ231273), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.87.3.215).

**Jameson, Narens, Goldfarb and Nelson 1990. The influence of near threshold priming on metamemory and recall.** Original experiment; abstract checked. Near-threshold answer primes improved recall without corresponding sensitivity in feeling-of-knowing judgments. This is a specific dissociation between a performance change and its monitor, not evidence that monitoring never helps. [Author paper](https://sites.socsci.uci.edu/~lnarens/1990/JamesonNarensGoldfarbNelson_Acta_Psychologica_1990.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0001-6918(90)90058-N).

**Maniscalco and Lau 2012. A signal detection theoretic approach for estimating metacognitive sensitivity from confidence ratings.** Original measurement method and application; abstract and introductory material checked. Meta-d′ estimates how confidence distinguishes correct from incorrect responses in task-comparable signal-detection units. It helps separate sensitivity from response bias. It is not a measure of wisdom or a test of whether a system is conscious; its modeling assumptions matter. [Corrected author PDF](https://brianmaniscalco.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Maniscalco-Lau-2012-Consc-Cog-corrected.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.concog.2011.09.021).

## Competing consciousness accounts

**Lau and Rosenthal 2011. Empirical support for higher order theories of conscious awareness.** Theory-led review advocating a higher-order account. Checked its introduction, theory comparison, and diagram discussion. Performance/report dissociations and prefrontal findings are interpreted as support, but do not uniquely identify the account. This is a theoretical position supported by selected evidence, not a decisive original experiment. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tics.2011.05.009).

**Rosenthal 2012. Higher order awareness misrepresentation and function.** Original philosophical argument; abstract and central sections checked. Explicitly distinguishes higher-order awareness proposed to explain consciousness from regulatory metacognition. Both may involve higher-order content and error, yet need not have the same function. The proposed limited utility of consciousness is the author's argument, not an established conclusion adopted here. [Full article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3318760/), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2011.0353).

**Lamme 2010. How neuroscience will change our view on consciousness.** Original theoretical target article drawing on earlier experiments, with published commentaries. Checked its distinctions among feedforward, local recurrent, and widespread recurrent processing and its concluding argument. It allows phenomenality without the higher-order access emphasized by rival accounts. Neural recurrence is not automatically a representation of a representation. The disagreement remains unresolved in this report. [Paper and commentaries](https://people.uncw.edu/tothj/PSY595/Lamme-How%20Neurosci%20Will%20Change%20Our%20View%20of%20Cs-CN-2010.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/17588921003731586).

The central disagreement concerns what explains experience, as distinct from reportability, confidence, or behavioral control. A task that measures one of the latter cannot be assumed to settle the former. This methodological conclusion is our synthesis of the competing positions.

## Observation can alter emotional processing

**Lieberman and colleagues 2007. Putting Feelings Into Words.** Original fMRI experiment with 30 participants. Full author-hosted paper checked, including methods and comparison conditions. Participants labeled expressions on faces; the study reports differences in amygdala activity across tasks. This is relevant to feedback from representational activity but does not test unbounded recursive self-modeling or provide a direct measure of subjective feeling. The proposed regional pathway draws partly on correlation and mediation. [Author paper](https://teams.semel.ucla.edu/sites/default/files/publications/May%202007%20-%20Putting%20Feelings%20Into%20Words.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01916.x).

**Levy-Gigi and Shamay-Tsoory 2022. Affect labeling The role of timing and intensity.** Original experiments; full paper checked. Experiment 2 compares labeling and control under two image-intensity conditions. Its outcome is reported distress, and generalization beyond the laboratory remains open. It provides a counterweight to universal downregulation claims. Labeling one's feelings here differs from labeling expressions on other faces in the preceding study. [Paper](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0279303).

## Computation self reference and deliberation

**Turing 1936–37. On Computable Numbers with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem.** Original formal work, with correction in the inspected copy. Universal simulation and diagonal arguments delimit effective procedures over a specified machine class. The original formulation concerns computable sequences and circle-free machines. It does not show that particular introspections are necessarily wrong or that finite bounded control problems are undecidable. [Stanford copy](https://theory.stanford.edu/~trevisan/cs172-07/turing36.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/s2-42.1.230).

**Jones 2013. A Swiss Pocket Knife for Computability.** Primary research on implementations, with a constructive exposition of Kleene's older self-reference theorem. Checked acceptable-language assumptions, the construction, and overhead discussion. The fixed point equates computed partial functions, not necessarily source text or terminating executions. Original Kleene scans were not successfully inspected, so Jones is identified as the checked exposition rather than the origin of the theorem. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5128), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4204/EPTCS.129.1).

**Russell and Wefald 1991. Principles of metareasoning.** Original normative computational framework. Publisher abstract checked; full article not inspected. Supports the historical attribution of evaluating computational actions through their effects on external decisions. The framework is not an empirical claim that people optimize expected computation value. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C).

**Hay, Russell, Tolpin and Shimony 2012. Selecting Computations Theory and Applications.** Original formal research; definitions, Theorems 4–7, and Example 3 checked. In its static selection model, bounded terminal utilities and constant positive computation cost yield a bound on optimal expected computation count and almost-sure stopping. There need be no uniform finite worst-case deadline. A positive myopic value supports continuing; the converse does not hold. The model does not directly cover reflection changing the target itself. [Full paper](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~russell/papers/uai12-meta.pdf), [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.5879).

**Wolpert 2008. Physical limits of inference.** Original formal research on inference devices defined over worldlines. Definitions and selected diagonal claims were checked, not every theorem. Universal success is obstructed under specified question, setup, and correctness conditions. Accurate restricted inference remains possible. Applying it to cognition requires defending those conditions; “embedded” alone supplies no universal failure theorem. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1362), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physd.2008.03.040).

**Lawvere 1969. Diagonal Arguments and Cartesian Closed Categories.** Original formal work; fixed-point argument checked in the scan. Under a strong representability premise, diagonalization gives a fixed point for each suitable endomap. Boolean negation then exposes a limit to that representability. This is not a convergence theorem for reflective psychology. [Original scan](https://www.its.caltech.edu/~matilde/LawvereDiagonalArgCartesianClosedCats.pdf), [Official reprint](https://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/reprints/articles/15/tr15abs.html).

## Information and abstraction

**Polyanskiy and Wu 2017. Strong data processing inequalities for channels and Bayesian networks.** Primary research developing stronger channel-dependent bounds. The checked abstract states the ordinary Markov-chain inequality used here; the synthesis supplies its elementary finite-variable proof directly. We do not apply the paper's stronger results to cognition. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.06025).

**Abel, Hershkowitz and Littman 2016. Near Optimal Behavior via Approximate State Abstraction.** Primary formal research on four abstraction families in Markov decision processes and corresponding performance bounds. This is relevant prior art for requiring assumptions before transferring performance across a representation. Our elementary deterministic closure proof is self-contained; their quantitative guarantees have not been imported into the feeling example. [Proceedings paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/abel16.html).

# Replacement and recurrent correction research record

This cycle executes the next target requested after the first structural-foundations study. It tests replacement of a correction interface, scaling with shared diagnostic capacity, and recurrent paid repair whose success restores the production funding later repairs.

Start with the [synthesis](synthesis.md). The main exact findings are:

- Hiding a cheap diagnostic raises robust correction reserve from three to four while preserving the plant graph and current output. A known invertible recoding preserves capacity.
- `n` independent hidden-fault modules with `k` parallel diagnostic channels need `ceil(n/k)+2` slots under the supplied three-stage protocol.
- A recurring route must finance each repair, finish in time, survive long quiet intervals, and replenish repair expense before the earliest next fault.
- In the base adaptive game, ready apparatus needs six initial units; absent apparatus needs sixteen, because two repairs can occur before the first replenishment. Another parameter regime favors suspension and rebuilding over permanent standby.

The universality claim supported here is conditional: the same proved constraint applies throughout its specified model class and under transformations that preserve its relevant structure. Empirical universality across real domains remains a hypothesis with explicit transfer tests.

# Modular replacement: same output and physical paths, different correction capacity

Completed exact model study, 5 October 2026. This executes the immediate modular milestone in the previous [research protocol](../next-research-target.md). It leaves the earlier files and the parent research workspace unchanged.

## Result

A replacement can preserve current operating output, every physical transition, all action costs and durations, and physical endpoint reachability while destroying a correction guarantee. The missing item is the decision interface. Conversely, a replacement that recodes both observations and commands through a known invertible adapter preserves the guarantee exactly.

In the model below, an original provider and its invertibly recoded replacement each require **three units of post-installation reserve** for guaranteed correction by tick three. A replacement that hides the cheap diagnostic result requires **four units** because a more expensive independent diagnostic remains available. At the matched reserve of three, physical reachability and full-information capacity are unchanged, but observation-feasible correction is lost. The best randomized guarantee there is success probability `1/2`.

This is a constructed conditional result using established control and information reasoning. It is not empirical evidence that actual replacements behave this way, nor a new universal law. Its value is an exact negative test for the proposed abstraction “same output and possible endpoints imply equivalent capacity.”

## 1. Two coupled components and a declared interface

The operating component has a hidden fixed condition `θ ∈ {0,1}` and a mode `old`, `renewed`, or `failed`. Applying revision `j` renews it exactly when `j=θ`; a mismatched revision causes irreversible failure. In old mode it delivers one service unit per tick during a grace interval ending at tick `H`. If it has not been renewed by `H`, it fails. Renewed mode is safe and absorbing for the correction test.

The revision component has a cash reserve `b`, a permit flag `p`, and a diagnostic register. It can inspect, test independently, obtain permission, and issue one of two implementation commands. Its steps are coupled to the operating component through the hidden condition and the implementation command.

**Output is not free financing.** The operating service consumes a separately supplied external feedstock; its one-unit output is a performance signal, never a deposit into the revision cash reserve. There is no cash replenishment during the test. Continued service after renewal remains conditional on that external feedstock. This module does not establish recurrent material self-renewal; the parallel recurrent study addresses a different question.

**Replacement price and timing.** All comparisons begin at the same completed handoff, with the same reserve and the same remaining grace interval. No claim of free installation is made. If each provider has the same prior installation fee `K ≥ 0`, the corresponding pre-installation reserve thresholds are `K+3` and `K+4`. A common installation delay must likewise be included before the three-tick correction interval, or subtracted from a common total deadline. Unequal installation costs or delays define a different comparison.

### State, actions, and chronology

The open plant state is

`q = (θ,t,b,p,s,r,m)`.

Here `s` identifies no diagnostic, cheap diagnostic, or fresh diagnostic; `r` is the diagnostic's internal raw bit, when present; and `m` is the operating mode. The controller sees the provider's interface, not the complete plant state. It has perfect recall of observations and its own commands. That memory is unpriced in this one-handoff milestone; paid forgetting is not claimed.

For every action, cash is paid first, the transition occurs in one tick, its observation is delivered, and the next decision is made. Costs and durations are distinct: the fresh diagnostic costs two units but still takes one tick.

| Action | Base cash cost | Effect |
|---|---:|---|
| Inspect provider | 1 | Writes the cheap diagnostic's internal result |
| Fresh independent test | 2 | Writes an independently accessible perfect diagnostic result |
| Authorize | 1 | Sets `p=1` |
| Apply 0 / apply 1 | 1 | Requires `p=1` in the authorized model; renews iff the physical revision matches `θ` |
| Wait | 0 | Uses one tick without changing the plant |

Insufficient cash disables an action. In the authorized comparison, a missing permit also disables implementation. The separate physical comparison removes only that authorization filter. Neither affordability nor permit status depends on `θ`. Repeated inspection, authorization, and waiting are allowed; this prevents a particular order from being hidden in the action grammar.

When an action reaches the deadline while leaving the plant old, the mode becomes failed. An incorrect implementation also fails immediately. After renewal, the verifier may stop because the target is safe and absorbing; its enumerated complete traces pad the remaining ticks with a zero-cash `hold`. Safety through `H` and safety until target attainment therefore agree here.

### Three providers

1. **Original.** Diagnostics store and display `θ`; command `apply j` physically applies revision `j`.
2. **Recoded replacement.** Diagnostics store and display `1−θ`; command `apply j` physically applies revision `1−j`. The adapter is known at handoff: flip the displayed bit, and flip implementation-command labels. Other observations and commands are unchanged. Providing and understanding this adapter belongs to the stipulated common handoff, not an unexplained discovery.
3. **Redacted replacement.** The underlying plant and diagnostic hardware are exactly those of the original, including the internal register `r=θ`. The interface displays a constant `redacted` after cheap inspection. A fresh independent test still displays `θ`. No controller is given secret access to the internal cheap-test bit.

The cheap signal is hidden before the replacement controller acquires it. We do not erase a fact while letting a perfect-recall controller continue to remember it. If a fresh diagnosis is acquired and a later cheap display hides it, perfect recall correctly preserves the earlier fresh diagnosis.

Time, reserve, permission, source label, operating mode, and current output are observable. Before a fresh diagnostic or final implementation, the redacted interface contains no condition-dependent side channel: action availability, fees, durations, permit observations, and refusal conditions are the same in both worlds. A final success/failure result can reveal the condition, but an error is already irreversible. No automatic “apply the internal bit” command is supplied; that would be an additional usable interface.

## 2. Positive result: a genuine interface-preserving replacement

**M1 — Exact policy transfer under the recoding.** The original and recoded systems have equal robust correction capacity for every tested initial reserve and horizon, and in fact for all nonnegative reserves and finite horizons under the declared rules.

Define a state map `φ` that leaves `θ,t,b,p,s,m` unchanged and flips the recoded raw register bit when a record is present. Define an action map `κ` that swaps `apply0` and `apply1` and leaves every other action unchanged. Define an observation map `η` that flips the displayed record bit and preserves the other fields.

These maps satisfy:

* initial states correspond under `φ`;
* `η(I_recoded(q)) = I_original(φ(q))`;
* action enabling, fees, one-tick duration, service output, safety, and target membership are preserved;
* `φ(step_recoded(q,κ(a))) = step_original(φ(q),a)` whenever the action is admitted.

The maps are involutions, so the same statements hold in reverse.

**Proof of capacity equivalence.** The adapter maps every received observation and issued command into a virtual original transcript. It runs the original controller on that transcript and translates its next command with `κ`. Induction on steps gives corresponding plant states, identical cash use, and identical deadline progress. Thus every original winning policy yields a recoded winning policy. The inverse adapter proves the converse. Its maintained transcript is within the explicitly permitted perfect-recall policy class. ∎

This is a concrete exact instance of the [previous sufficient refinement criterion](../formal-foundations.md), with costs and timing preserved rather than merely bounded. It uses established [alternating-refinement reasoning](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~alur/Concur98.html). No inference from similar-looking outputs is needed: the correspondence is exhibited transition by transition.

## 3. Negative result: even the full plant graph can omit the decisive fact

**M2 — Physical graph equality does not imply observation-feasible equivalence.** The original and redacted providers have exactly the same open plant transition graph, for both the physical and authorized action interpretations. They therefore have the same possible action/state trajectories, current service output, cash accounting, and physical endpoint reachability. Their correction capacities differ.

Graph equality is immediate: `provider=redacted` changes the observation function only; it does not occur in the state-transition clauses. This statement deliberately concerns the plant graph with its observation interface omitted. The two complete partially observed systems are not equal: their diagnostic messages differ.

### Exact thresholds and proof

Let the cheap diagnostic cost be `α>0`, fresh diagnostic cost `β>0`, permission cost `γ>0`, and implementation cost `δ>0`, with all durations still one tick. Assume the same initial state: no diagnosis acquired, no permit, and hidden `θ` admitting both possibilities.

For `H≥3`, minimum robust reserve is

`B_original = B_recoded = min(α,β)+γ+δ`,

`B_redacted = β+γ+δ`.

No robust correction policy exists for `H<3`, regardless of reserve, because an informative diagnostic, authorization, and implementation each need a separate tick in this architecture. Permission and diagnosis may occur in either order.

**Sufficiency:** use the least expensive informative diagnostic, authorize, and implement the indicated revision. The original and recoded providers can use either diagnostic; the redacted provider uses the fresh one. Each path prepays its own fees and takes three ticks.

**Necessity:** every authorized successful path pays `γ` for permission and `δ` for final implementation. A sure policy for both hidden conditions must acquire a distinguishing signal before its first implementation: before such a signal it must issue the same distribution of commands in both worlds, and the two worlds require incompatible irreversible implementations. Only an informative diagnostic can create that distinction. For the redacted provider that means a fresh test costing `β`; the original and recoded providers pay at least `min(α,β)`. These expenses occur on the same successful path and add. Repeated operations and waiting cannot reduce them. ∎

At base prices `(α,β,γ,δ)=(1,2,1,1)`, the robust thresholds are therefore **3, 3, and 4**. Full-information authorized correction needs `γ+δ=2` units and two ticks for every provider; full-information physical correction needs `δ=1` unit and one tick. A favorable successful physical path exists for each hidden condition in every provider even when a common observation-based policy cannot guarantee it.

At reserve three and deadline three, the redacted provider's maximum worst-case randomized success is exactly `1/2`. A fair guess after authorization attains it. For an upper bound, any successful policy branch that buys a fresh diagnostic would also need permission and implementation, costing four; at reserve three such a branch cannot complete. Hence successful implementation has no usable information about `θ`. Its success probabilities in the two worlds sum to at most one, so their minimum is at most one half. This also exposes the difference between impossibility of a guarantee and inevitability of failure on every run.

### Controls that delimit the mechanism

* If the fresh diagnostic becomes as cheap as the cheap diagnostic, the replacement gap disappears: both thresholds are `3` at unit permission and implementation costs.
* If `θ` is supplied in advance, every provider has the same two-unit authorized threshold. The effect is informational, not a different physical repair technology or entitlement.
* With four units and three ticks, the redacted provider succeeds through its independent substitute. The example does not obtain a permanent impossibility by deleting all alternatives.
* If time is too short, every provider fails the robust test, even with ample cash. Extra reserve does not purchase nonexistent time in this action architecture.
* All providers start with the same post-installation reserve and service performance. Operating output never pays a diagnostic fee in the calculation.

## 5. What can transfer across scale, space, or time

The supported claim is **invariance under specified structure-preserving changes**, not universality under arbitrary change of scale.

Changing cash units by a positive factor, while multiplying every price and initial reserve by that same factor, preserves affordability and the policy correspondence. The script checks factors `1,2,5`; the general proof is `kb≥kc` iff `b≥c` for `k>0`, followed by induction on the ledger. Similarly, relabeling locations or carrier identities preserves this model only when the transition and information interfaces are transported with the labels. This model contains no spatial geometry and establishes no physical spatial-scaling law.

Uniformly rescaling every action duration and deadline preserves this finite model's order of decisions and observations. Changing only some delays, revealing a diagnostic later, or allowing a new simultaneous operation can change the threshold. These are mechanism changes, not unit changes.

**M3 — Temporal aggregation can erase feedback.** Keep the original provider and the same possible three-step microtrajectories, but require all three commands to be committed before any diagnostic result is delivered. At reserve three, no such open-loop batch can guarantee correction; its best worst-case success is `1/2`. The checked adaptive policy can guarantee success. The batch can contain inspection, but its final command cannot depend on that result. An aggregate description that retains an internal feedback controller would be a different, potentially faithful abstraction.

This gives a direct criterion for the scale conjecture: identify what transformations of description preserve causal order, information access, action authority, resource timing, and the test being assessed. The successful recoding is a positive witness. Redaction and feedback-losing batching are counterexamples to broader equivalence claims. A similar phenomenon in human coordination, AI systems, or biology still requires an independently justified correspondence of mechanisms; the shared terminology does not supply one.

## 6. Decision for the next step

The modular milestone is complete: it gives an interface-preserving replacement theorem, a stronger-than-output-matching counterexample, explicit substitutes, exact thresholds, and reproducible checks. The new result does not require a larger ontology.

The next integration question is whether a recurrent productive-and-corrective loop can be abstracted without losing the interfaces exposed here. Candidate summaries should be challenged with replacements that preserve current output and total reserves but alter when evidence can guide enactment. The parallel recurrent model should report which of its invariants survive the good adapter and which fail under the redacted or delayed interface, while separately accounting for installation, memory, standby, and restart.

No statement here makes persistence or increased correction capacity ethically good by itself. The protected service, irreversible-failure convention, and duty to correct are declared features of the test. Their legitimacy and their adequacy for affected people remain separate questions.

# Recurrent paid repair: an exact finite model

5 October 2026. This study executes the recurrent-repair target in a deliberately small model. It derives a reserve–delay–disturbance-spacing frontier for two prescribed routes, solves the full allowed finite control game, and preserves both winning controllers and losing counterstrategies. Infinite guarantees follow from invariants and a greatest fixed point, not from long simulated survival.

The results are conditional mathematical constructions. The action grammar, costs, perfect diagnostics, protected service duty, and disturbance class are supplied. They neither establish a universal preference for standby nor solve alignment. No files in the parent research workspace were changed.

## 1. What the model makes endogenous

A productive function yields support only while healthy. Every new fault stops that output. A successful diagnosis, authorization, and implementation restores the function; without repair, its support source does not continue producing in the background. Investigation apparatus can be retained in paid standby, suspended, rebuilt while healthy, rebuilt after a fault, or replaced by a paid alternative diagnostic provider in a control case.

What remains fixed is just as consequential. The possible faults and repairs are a supplied binary grammar. Passive fault detection is immediate and free. There are no competing purposes, strategic manipulation, noisy reports, or discovered new interpretations. The apparatus is **diagnostic-specific**: it is not the whole institution and is not required for authorization or implementation once the needed bit is known.

## 2. Parameters and exact chronology

Primitive output, fees, reserves, and delays below are nonnegative integers. Operating cost and the deadline are positive integers, and episode cost is positive in the theorems. The derived net surplus `p` and net cycle balances may be negative.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `B` | Maximum reserve carried from one slot to the next |
| `b₀` | Initial accessible reserve, independently varied from zero to `B` |
| `y` | Gross healthy-slot support output, requiring supplied external feedstock |
| `c` | Operating support spent in every slot, including outage slots |
| `p=y−c` | Healthy net output before apparatus expense |
| `m` | Standby expense for carrying a ready diagnostic apparatus through a healthy slot |
| `K,L` | Rebuilding fee and extra fault slots before a rebuilt apparatus can diagnose |
| `d,a,x` | Diagnostic, authorization, and implementation fees |
| `Δ` | Minimum separation between fault onsets, measured in slots |
| `D` | Maximum permitted outage duration for each fault |

The state at a slot boundary contains reserve, elapsed time since the previous onset (clipped at `Δ`), current healthy/diagnose/authorize/execute phase, completed fault-slot count, and apparatus status. The apparatus is absent, ready, or rebuilding with an integer remaining delay. The fixed-fault control also carries a free remembered diagnostic bit.

Each slot has the following order:

1. If the function is healthy and at least `Δ` slots have elapsed since its previous onset, the environment may cause a new fault or remain quiet. A first fault may occur immediately at the initial boundary. The occurrence of a fault is publicly visible before the controller acts. Its cause `θ∈{0,1}` is hidden.
2. A quiet healthy slot produces `y` support units from the declared external feedstock. Every fault slot, including the slot in which repair completes, produces zero.
3. The controller selects its action using the visible event, state, and any acquired diagnostic report. Current receipts are available before current operating expense and action fees. The action is unaffordable if these available funds cannot pay it.
4. Rebuilding and the selected action complete their one-slot progress. Diagnosis reveals the current bit; authorization and implementation each require their own later slot. A correct implementation restores health at the end of its slot. A wrong implementation would fail irreversibly.
5. Remaining funds above `B` are spilled, and clocks update. Output resumes only in the next healthy slot. An unresolved fault after its `D`th slot is a violation; completion exactly in that slot is allowed.

The transaction identity is checked on every generated affordable transition:

`b_after + operating + fee + spill = b_before + gross_receipt`.

**Cap convention:** `B` caps carried reserve after receipts and billing. Current receipts can flow directly to current expenses before surplus is deposited or spilled. It is not a hard bound on the instantaneous amount of cash immediately after a gross receipt. Imposing such a peak bound or moving output after payment would define a different model and could change the reserve thresholds. Fault-period fees never use future restored output.

During healthy periods, absent apparatus can remain absent or start a proactive rebuild. A ready apparatus can be suspended without a refund or retained at cost `m`. An unfinished rebuild can continue or be cancelled. Completing a rebuild in a healthy slot incurs that slot's ready-carry fee. During faults, local rebuilding incurs `K` at its start and `L` extra zero-output slots; if `L=0`, rebuilding and the diagnostic occur in the same slot. Authorization and execution remain separate. At execution, the controller can retain or suspend the apparatus for future episodes.

New faults occur only while healthy; they do not interrupt an already unresolved fault. Under an earliest-onset adversary, a repair lasting `τ` slots is followed by exactly

`g(τ)=max(0,Δ−τ)`

healthy earning slots. If `τ≥Δ`, the next fault can start immediately after recovery and there is no healthy earning interval.

### Information and memory

Every ordinary episode has a fresh hidden bit, unconstrained by earlier bits. This is an adversarial uncertainty class, not an iid probability assertion. Seeing that output stopped reveals the onset but not the correct repair. The diagnostic supplies a perfect report. A realizable controller retains its reported bit through authorization and applies that reported repair. Its storage is explicitly free in this first model.

The solver collapses the two report values into one symmetric information state. Before diagnosis the two causes share the same available action; after diagnosis, their continuation graphs are isomorphic under exchanging `apply 0` and `apply 1`. The abstract action `apply_reported` means the concrete rule `apply(report)`. It is not an oracle that sees the hidden cause. Incorrect guesses cannot provide a sure guarantee and are not added as winning alternatives. The fixed supplied workflow requires diagnosis, then authorization, then implementation; it does not claim all real repair processes have this order.

The environment's observable branch is **fault versus quiet**, never `θ=0` versus `θ=1`. Consequently the predecessor order `for every observed event, there exists a controller response` does not leak the hidden cause. A free finite report register suffices for the witness controller; allowing perfect recall supplies no information about unconstrained fresh future bits.

## 3. Exact route frontier

These theorems concern local diagnostics required anew every episode, an always available authorization service at the stated per-episode fee, no alternative provider, and positive episode expense. The no-hazard, full-information, and retained-fixed-bit cases are separate controls.

### Route S: keep a ready apparatus in paid standby

Start with the apparatus ready. Always retain it, diagnose each fault immediately, then authorize and implement. Put

`τ_S=3`, `C_S=3c+d+a+x`, `g_S=max(0,Δ−τ_S)`.

The route satisfies the indefinite service-and-budget duty against every admitted disturbance history **if and only if**

`b₀≥C_S`, `B≥C_S`, `τ_S≤D`, `p−m≥0`, and `g_S(p−m)≥C_S`.

When these conditions hold, the least initial credit for this **ready** start is `C_S`.

### Route R: remain suspended while healthy and rebuild after a fault

Start with the apparatus absent. Never rebuild or maintain it while healthy; rebuild immediately on each fault, diagnose, authorize, implement, and suspend again. Put

`τ_R=L+3`, `C_R=K+(L+3)c+d+a+x`, `g_R=max(0,Δ−τ_R)`.

The route satisfies the same duty **if and only if**

`b₀≥C_R`, `B≥C_R`, `τ_R≤D`, `p≥0`, and `g_R p≥C_R`.

Its least initial credit for this **cold** start is `C_R`. No larger finite reserve repairs a violated recurrent-flow inequality: additional credit can only postpone exhaustion. Immediate rebuild is best within this reserve-only route, since fault-period delay generates neither income nor additional information. The unrestricted game below additionally permits proactive healthy-period rebuilding and suspension choices, so the route comparison is not presented as the global optimum.

### Proof of both claims

Let `C,τ,g` be the chosen route's episode expense, duration, and minimum healthy gap, and let `q` be its healthy net accumulation rate (`p−m` or `p`). A first immediate fault requires `b₀≥C`; a recurrent episode requires the storage bound `B≥C`. Since every fault expense is paid before any restored output, this total also suffices for every prefix of that fixed repair sequence. Duration must not exceed `D`.

If `q≥0` and `gq≥C`, the reserve at successive onsets satisfies

`b_next = min(B, b_onset−C+hq) ≥ C`, for every `h≥g` and `b_onset≥C`.

Thus onset reserve at least `C` is an inductive invariant. Healthy delays cannot reduce it. Every fault is completed within `τ≤D`, and all intermediate bills are affordable. This proves the infinite guarantee, including histories with indefinitely many faults and histories that eventually remain quiet.

Conversely, if `q<0`, an arbitrarily long quiet interval exhausts every finite reserve under that prescribed route. If `gq<C`, an adversary choosing each earliest allowed onset creates a strict deficit each cycle; finite reserve is eventually exhausted. If the deadline fails, the first fault cannot be completed on time. The storage and initial-credit failures follow from the unpaid episode prefix. This exhausts the stated cases.

With authority supplied freely and instantaneously, the same local-diagnostic argument removes the authorization slot and fee: `τ_S=2`, `C_S=2c+d+x`; add `L` slots and `K+Lc` for the cold route. The implementation checks this variant as well. The analytic helper explicitly refuses full-information, fixed-bit, and alternative-provider configurations, whose routes differ.

## 4. Exact game over all allowed apparatus decisions

The unrestricted controller can keep, suspend, initiate a proactive rebuild, continue or cancel it, rebuild during a fault, and retain or release the apparatus after repair. The alternative-provider control also permits paid external diagnosis. No comparison assumes the controller must preserve the incumbent.

For each fixed `B` the graph is finite. It records cash `0,…,B`, clipped onset clock, finite repair phase and deadline age, finite rebuild delay, and the fixed-bit memory flag where relevant. All initial credits and both initial apparatus states are included in one solved graph.

Let `W` be the greatest set such that, for every state in `W` and every admitted **observable** environment event, at least one affordable controller action has its successor in `W` and does not miss a deadline. This is the greatest fixed point of the safety predecessor, computed by eliminating states whose environment can force all controller replies outside the current set.

**Why this certifies indefinite recurrent repair.** Select one surviving action for each state and event. The exported finite controller keeps the state in `W` forever. Since an unfinished fault violates safety after `D` slots, the controller must finish every onset within that deadline; it cannot preserve safety by waiting forever. Quiet states continue the specified operating process. This is a proof by a finite inductive invariant.

For every eliminated state, the program also exports an environment event for which **every** controller reply either violates a constraint immediately or enters a strictly smaller losing rank. That rank decreases to a violation in finitely many steps. It proves the negative side and the minimum initial credits, rather than merely reporting that one searched controller failed.

The environment can choose onset times adaptively from the current state subject to the spacing rule. The solver does not enumerate only stationary disturbance patterns. There is no stochastic almost-sure inference or simulation extrapolation.

The controller's selected action within the winning set is a witness, not an optimized long-run burden policy. A lower current fee is used only to break ties. Capacity and burden should not be conflated.

Each number is the exact least initial credit among **all allowed policies** for the stated initial apparatus. “None” means every initial credit through the declared cap loses; where an analytic argument proves failure for every finite cap, that is stated separately.

### Base: a bridge reserve is larger than either repair bill

With ready apparatus, a fault costs six and lasts three slots. The two healthy slots before the next earliest onset each accumulate `p−m=3`, restoring the six. Thus reserve six and storage cap six suffice indefinitely for standby.

Cold rebuilding costs ten and lasts five slots. In the base spacing class, an earliest next fault begins immediately on completion. A pure suspend-and-rebuild route therefore pays ten repeatedly with no healthy output and fails with **every finite reserve**.

An adaptive cold-start controller can rebuild once and then keep the apparatus. Its first repair costs ten, followed immediately by a ready repair costing six. No healthy receipt lies between them. Hence **sixteen** initial units are necessary, independently of the solver. Sixteen are sufficient: after these two repairs, the apparatus is ready and the ordinary two-slot healthy gap restores six for each later ready repair. A longer quiet interval adds nonnegative support. This is a startup bridge requirement, not a steady-state repair cost.

This comparison treats initial assets honestly: a ready apparatus is an endowed noncash asset. Ready and cold columns are not said to be matched total wealth. Within each column all compared policies receive the same starting state and cash. Proactive building and its actual fee and delay are part of the game.

### Opposite regime: standby is not always the solution

For `p=3,m=4,K=1,L=1,Δ=7,D=4`, forced standby spends one more unit than it earns on every quiet slot, so an arbitrarily long quiet interval defeats it for any finite reserve.

A suspended episode costs eight, lasts four slots, and is followed by at least three healthy earning slots. Those yield nine, so suspended repair is indefinitely feasible with cold initial credit eight and cap at least eight. From an initially ready state, credit six suffices: an immediate first fault uses the endowed apparatus; subsequent operation can suspend and rebuild. If the first slot is quiet and the on-demand controller suspends, its three units of net output already raise credit six to at least the eight needed for a cold fault. These are distinct histories that the same policy must handle.

**Storage and initial credit are not interchangeable.** The full game verifies:

| Regime and storage cap | Least ready credit | Least cold credit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Base, `B=6` | 6 | None |
| Base, `B=15` | 6 | None |
| Base, `B=16` | 6 | 16 |
| Expensive standby, `B=6` | None | None |
| Expensive standby, `B=7` | None | None |
| Expensive standby, `B=8` | 6 | 8 |

The last three rows include proactive rebuilding and every other allowed apparatus policy, not merely a comparison of two fixed schedules.

### Controls that distinguish mechanisms

**Known cause and fixed cause differ initially.** When every new cause is supplied, only authorization and implementation remain, costing four over two slots. With a constant initially unknown cause, the first diagnosis still costs money and time. Thereafter a free retained bit makes the recurrent problem identical to the known-cause version for its relevant phase. The cold initial threshold fourteen equals the ten-unit initial cold repair plus an immediately following four-unit informed repair. The diagnostic apparatus can then be discarded, while per-episode authority and execution remain necessary. Thus the control does not falsely erase all corrective needs when information is free.

**A substitute can be better than rebuilding the incumbent.** The external diagnostic surcharge makes an apparatus-free episode cost eight over three slots. Two healthy slots at net four replace that cost exactly. Hence cold initial credit eight works without rebuilding local apparatus. The forced-standby class needs nine from cold in this control because it spends some recovery income establishing and maintaining the local apparatus; preserving that particular provider is not the protected objective.

**The spacing violation is substantive.** At `Δ=4`, each fault requires at least three zero-output slots and six support units. There is at most one healthy earning slot before the next earliest onset, worth at most four before any apparatus fees. Thus every cycle loses at least two units even under this optimistic bound. No finite reserve can sustain the specified service against that onset pattern; this strengthens the numerical cap-24 negative result.

**The external boundary is indispensable.** With `y=0`, every slot consumes at least one and receives nothing. Finite initial reserve fails regardless of the policy. The positive results assume a reliable, indefinitely supplied external feedstock that the healthy productive function converts to the stated support output. The alternative-provider control similarly assumes that paid diagnostic service remains available. Neither model closes the entire physical economy.

**No hazard is not an ineffective-repair case.** If no fault is admitted, there is no recurring correction duty. A controller can suspend the apparatus, earn `p`, and perform no investigation. Forced standby is also feasible in the base prices but pays a needless unit each quiet slot. The model therefore does not make inquiry permanent by definition.

The completed result is an exact conditional separation: money, maintained diagnostic access, rebuild latency, inherited information, and outside provider access can substitute for one another in some regions and fail to substitute in others. A favorable recurrent balance is insufficient without a payable initial bridge and deadline compatibility. Conversely, paying indefinitely to keep a particular diagnostic apparatus can be worse than suspending it or replacing its service.

The proofs use established accounting and finite safety-game reasoning. No mathematical novelty is claimed. The positive recurrence statement is relative to an explicitly bounded disturbance class and an external feedstock assumption. The protected duty—keep operating when healthy and repair every admitted fault by `D`—is supplied; the model does not determine whether this duty is ethical, whether the outputs are beneficial, or who should bear the costs.
